publisher: US Army Historical Division (NARA M1035, Fold3 images)
license_or_status: Work of the US Government (Foreign Military Studies programme); public domain in the United States. German text paraphrased in English in the claims.
reliability_note: not an independent source: same FMS family as the other manuscripts and as R2217, the 20 September 1944 report of the same corps headquarters signed in draft by the same author (one family: same author and staff, and the copy reaches us only inside the FMS file; R2216 and R2217 never raise each other or any other FMS row, and either raises an agreeing row of another family). short_title: AHQ Report No. 57, Major Changes in Army Organization, 1939-1945
full_citation: Historical Section (G.S.), Army Headquarters, Report No. 57: A Summary of Major Changes in Army Organization, 1939-1945 (22 December 1952); Directorate of History and Heritage, Department of National Defence, electronic version, ahq057.pdf. Appendix C is the authorized composition of a Canadian infantry division as at 31 May 1945 (C.A.O.R.O. 5941, 4 July 1945, Schedule A): 917 officers and 17,158 other ranks (18,075) for the 1st Canadian Infantry Division and 917 and 17,176 (18,093) for the 2nd and 3rd. Appendix D is the authorized composition of a Canadian armoured division as at the same date: 742 officers and 13,837 other ranks (14,579) for the 4th Canadian Armoured Division and 748 and 14,033 (14,781) for the 5th. Appendix E is the authorized composition of an independent armoured brigade (180 officers and 3,376 other ranks). The narrative states that Canadian formations were organized on British war establishments, with a reorganization effective 11 January 1943. The cover leaf states that the report is a preliminary narrative and should not be regarded as authoritative.
publisher: Directorate of History and Heritage, Department of National Defence (canada.ca)
license_or_status: Crown copyright (Government of Canada); DHH electronic version of an unpublished Historical Section report; only short facts are used, paraphrased
reliability_note: Official Canadian Historical Section (G.S.) report compiled from CMHQ/AHQ files, war establishments and Canadian Army Overseas Routine Orders. The cover leaf warns that the report is preliminary and has not been checked for accuracy in all aspects. These are Canadian authorized compositions on British-pattern tables as at 31 May 1945, not a British 1944 Personnel Staff Table; the infantry totals (18,075-18,093) disagree with the 18,347 figure in Nafziger 939BXIA.
